title: What we have handled (1 John 1:1–4)
hookLine: the word of life that we have seen and touched

lines: A COLD WAVE OVER YOUR FEET.
I WAS THERE. I TOUCHED HIM.
cards: You can read everything about the ocean, tides, salt, the color of deep water, and watch it in videos for hours.
Then one day you stand at the edge and a cold wave runs over your feet, and the water teaches what the books couldn't. Hearing about it, seeing it, touching it: three different kinds of knowing.
The first letter of John doesn't open with a greeting or a name. It opens with a witness, an old man, as tradition pictures him, saying: I'm not passing on a rumor. I was there.

teach.b: Listen to the sentence move, in the Douay-Rheims: "That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the word of life."
It starts at the very start of everything, from the beginning, an echo of the opening of John's Gospel. Then it comes closer, step by step. Heard: across a room.
Looked upon: a long, steady gaze. And handled: hands on. The Word that was with God from the beginning is something a fisherman could put his hand on.
Why insist? Some scholars think the letter was answering people who said Jesus only seemed to have a body, that God would never really take on flesh, get tired, bleed. John won't have it.

teach.h: NOT A GHOST: COME IN THE FLESH.
teach.b: Later in the letter he says that every spirit which confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God.
The Greek word for handled is the same one the risen Jesus uses in Luke's Gospel, when the frightened disciples think he's a spirit: handle, and see.
And notice why John writes: so that you may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son. The Greek is koinonia, which comes into Catholic language as communion.
And so that our joy may be full.

teach.h: OUR HANDS HAVE HANDLED THE WORD OF LIFE.
teach.b: For Catholics this touchable faith runs through the sacraments: water on a forehead, oil on hands, bread placed on a tongue or in a palm. God, in this tradition, keeps coming close enough to touch.

how: Catholic sacraments are celebrated with things that can be seen and touched, water, oil, bread, wine and the laying on of hands, and Catholics may keep a rosary, cross or medal close as a physical reminder of their faith.

o: fellowship, sharing a life in common
a meal eaten only by the clergy
a church building where people gather

games.q: what we have handled — tap the pairs.

s: 1 John opens with a greeting and the writer's name
it opens with a witness: what we have heard, seen, looked upon and handled.
the letter insists Jesus came in the flesh
some scholars think it answers people who said he only seemed to have a body.
the Greek word for handled is also used by the risen Jesus in Luke
handle, and see: he is not a spirit.

games.q: someone in your community says Jesus only seemed to have a body, that God would never really take on flesh. you're the writer of 1 John. how do you answer?
o: agree: spirit matters more than flesh.
say plainly: our hands have handled him.
games.why: the letter opens with exactly that: heard, seen, looked upon, handled. later it says whoever confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God.

practice: Hold something near you, a cross, a rosary, a smooth stone, or just your own palm, and feel its weight, its temperature, its edges. Let it stand for a faith that says God came close enough to touch.
If you pray, hold it as a prayer without words; if not, stay with the plain fact of touch and notice what your hands know.

wordCard.voice: Koinonia, fellowship. First John one: the word of life, heard, seen, looked upon and touched, so that we may share this fellowship together. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: (our hands) have handled (1 John 1:1). from psēlaphaō, to touch, to feel.

carryVoice: Your line: seen and touched. Heard, seen, looked upon, and handled by human hands. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the word of life
